\section[spingere]{spingere — to push}

\label{lesson:IT-C240-spingere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to give back, then the Italian for to recognise.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: spingere}
\textbf{spingere} — \textquotedblleft{}to push\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{spingere} $\leftarrow$ Vulgar Latin \emph{expingere}, from \emph{ex-} and \emph{pangere}, \textquotedblleft{}to fix, to drive in\textquotedblright{} — inherited. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}

\section[superare]{superare — to overtake, to pass}

\label{lesson:IT-C240-superare}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: superare}
\textbf{superare} — \textquotedblleft{}to overtake, to pass\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{superare} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{superare}, \textquotedblleft{}to go over, to rise above\textquotedblright{} — a learned borrowing. EtymDB 2.1 has no row for \emph{superare}; it derives Spanish and Portuguese \emph{superar}, borrowed the same way, from \emph{superare}.

\section[svolgere]{svolgere — to perform, to carry out}

\label{lesson:IT-C240-svolgere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to waste, then the Italian for to overtake.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: svolgere}
\textbf{svolgere} — \textquotedblleft{}to perform, to carry out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{svolgere} is \emph{s-}, \textquotedblleft{}out\textquotedblright{}, plus \emph{volgere}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}: to unroll, to carry out. \emph{volgere} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{volvere}, \textquotedblleft{}to roll\textquotedblright{}. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}
